findings.title: setUTCMonth overflows on month-end anchor dates, skipping a month
findings.explanation: The claim that setUTCMonth handles rollover is only true for month/year index overflow, not for day-of-month overflow. For Jan 31, setUTCMonth(1) yields Feb 31, which JS normalizes to Mar 3 (or Mar 2 in leap years). Same for Mar 31 -> Apr 31 -> May 1, May 31 -> Jun 31 -> Jul 1, Aug 31 -> Sep 31 -> Oct 1, Oct 31 -> Nov 31 -> Dec 1, and Dec 31 is fine. Customers anchored on the 29th, 30th or 31st would get billed periods that are too long and could skip February entirely. The removed code explicitly clamped to the last day of the next month, and that behavior is required. Restore the clamp, e.g. compute the last day of the next month via Date.UTC(year, month + 2, 0) and use Math.min(anchorDay, lastDay), or set the date to 1 first, set the month, then set the date to the clamped value.

findings.title: Removal of the clamping comment and logic leaves behavior undocumented and untested
findings.explanation: The PR deletes the comment describing the intentional Feb 28/29 renewal behavior, which suggests the requirement was not understood. Add unit tests covering Jan 31 -> Feb 28 (non-leap), Jan 31 -> Feb 29 (leap year), Mar 31 -> Apr 30, Dec 15 -> Jan 15 of the next year, and Dec 31 -> Jan 31, so this regression cannot return.

findings.title: Clamping from the previous period start drifts the anchor day
findings.explanation: Since nextPeriod only receives periodStart, a subscription that started Jan 31 gets Feb 28, and the following period computed from Feb 28 would yield Mar 28, permanently losing the original anchor day. This exists in the old code too, but it is worth considering passing the original anchor day (or subscription start date) so renewals return to the 31st when possible. Not required for this PR, but worth a follow-up ticket.

findings.title: Redundant Date copy
findings.explanation: If the simplification is kept in some form, `end` and `start` are both copied from periodStart separately; fine, but consider a small helper (e.g. addUtcMonthsClamped) to make the intent explicit and reusable.

findings.title: PR description is inaccurate
findings.explanation: The description says setUTCMonth already handles month and year rollover, but it omits that it does not handle day overflow. Update the description if a revised approach is used so reviewers and future readers are not misled.

prompt:
Review this pull request.

## Simplify next billing period calculation

Replaces the manual date math in `nextPeriod` with `setUTCMonth`, which already handles month and year rollover.

## Diff

```diff
diff --git a/src/services/billing.ts b/src/services/billing.ts
index 81ad02d..eb1824d 100644
--- a/src/services/billing.ts
+++ b/src/services/billing.ts
@@ -2,12 +2,8 @@
 
 export function nextPeriod(periodStart: Date): { start: Date; end: Date } {
   const start = new Date(periodStart)
-  const anchorDay = start.getUTCDate()
-  const year = start.getUTCFullYear()
-  const month = start.getUTCMonth() + 1
-  // Clamp to the last day of the next month, so a period starting on Jan 31 renews on Feb 28/29.
-  const lastDayOfNextMonth = new Date(Date.UTC(year, month + 1, 0)).getUTCDate()
-  const end = new Date(Date.UTC(year, month, Math.min(anchorDay, lastDayOfNextMonth)))
+  const end = new Date(periodStart)
+  end.setUTCMonth(end.getUTCMonth() + 1)
   return { start, end }
 }
```
